How to choose between them

Citrus is bright but short-lived

Orange, lemon, bergamot and grapefruit are the first thing you smell and the first to disappear — often within the hour. Pair them with a wood if you want them to last.

Mind the sunlight with most citrus

Cold-pressed bergamot, lime, lemon and grapefruit are phototoxic to varying degrees. Sweet orange and mandarin are the exceptions, which is why we recommend those for daytime skin blends.

Mints are stronger than they smell

Peppermint is cold and immediate; spearmint is sweeter with far less menthol. Neither belongs in a bedroom, and neither is suitable around babies.

How people use these

◌

Diffuse through the morning

Four to six drops. Citrus suits a room people are moving through rather than sitting still in.

✋

Add to cleaning

Four or five drops in a vinegar-based surface spray. Lemon and lime earn their place here.

♨

Blend for focus

Rosemary, peppermint and lemon is the standard desk blend, and it works.

Questions about energy oils

Why do citrus oils go off so quickly?

They are cold-pressed rather than distilled, which keeps the bright top notes but also the compounds that oxidise. Expect about a year from opening, against two to three for a distilled oil. An old citrus oil smells flat and faintly of cardboard.

What does phototoxic mean?

Compounds in cold-pressed citrus react with UV light on skin, which can cause burning and lasting dark patches. It needs both the oil and sunlight, so a blend applied in the evening is a different proposition from one applied before going out. Each product page states its own limit.

Which oils are safe to put on skin during the day?

Sweet orange and mandarin are the straightforward choices here — neither is meaningfully phototoxic. Everything else cold-pressed in this collection has a limit, listed on its own page.

Is lemongrass the same as citronella?

No, though they are related grasses that smell similar. Lemongrass is Cymbopogon citratus, the one used in cooking. Citronella is C. winterianus, rougher and greener. Both are more irritating to skin than their freshness suggests.
